failure_modes: Horizon so short that endgame defection appears
Stated horizon that contradicts what actually happens erodes trust in later instructions
gloss: A known finite horizon raises the effort an agent spends per step
invariants: The horizon is stated to the agent, not merely implied
Perceived duration changes the agent's care per step
mechanism: Telling an agent that a role lasts many rounds, or that it will end at a known time, makes it treat each step as consequential. Effort scales with the perceived stake of the whole horizon, even when only one round is actually executed.
